With the midterm elections just weeks away, President Donald Trump’s approval rating is underwater in a super-majority of states, according to new polling.

In a new state-by-state tracker from Civiqs, an online polling firm, more registered voters disapproved than approved of Trump’s job performance in 39 states.

results.content: In the closing weeks before the November 3 US congressional midterm elections, 80 percent of Americans polled said the country needs substantial change or “complete and total upheaval” in how it is run, according to the survey of over 1,100 US adults released on Thursday. Democrats and independents are much more likely than Republicans to want a total overhaul of the country’s direction, the survey found, but even Republican voters are still looking for some change. Fuelled by soaring living costs, everyday economics is driving a majority of the electorate, with 85 percent of respondents saying the economy is one of the most significant issues in weighing their vote in the upcoming election.
results.title: Ahead of US midterms, voters are frustrated with Trump, want change: Poll - Al Jazeera

results.content: With less than two weeks to go before the congressional elections, Americans are nearly as gloomy about the economy as they were when the nation was emerging from the pandemic, and President Donald Trump's economic approval rating is hitting an all-time low, according to the latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey. Overall, 63% of the public is pessimistic about the current state of the economy and the outlook, up 1 percentage point from the July survey. But that percentage now includes 35% of Republicans, up 6 points from July and the highest level of Republican pessimism of either of Trump's two terms.
